description: This paper by Karl Kim and Lily Bui, published in the International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction in 2019, examines why island communities face different response and recovery problems from continental ones when supply chains are disrupted: isolation, limited port capacity, lack of alternative facilities and dependence on imports raise their vulnerability. It connects supply chain management literature with disaster risk, recovery and resilience; compares the island supply chains of Puerto Rico and Hawaii, which face similar hazards and geographic isolation; and draws tactical, operational and strategic actions from Hurricane Maria's impacts on Puerto Rico for emergency managers and planners in islands and other isolated places. A key lesson is the importance of communications and coordination in restoring lifelines, networks and social relations after disasters. Coverage: Puerto Rico and Hawaii. Access: journal article. Licence and cost: subscription. Caveats: a qualitative analysis based on the abstract read, without port throughput data. It informs emergency response and resilience planning for port-dependent supply chains. It relates to the post-hurricane supply chain case study of Harvey, Irma and Maria and the NOAA Harvey port reopening case in the catalogue.
